title: Wipro, CrowdStrike Launch CISO Command Center for AI-Era Security
excerpt: The joint offering pairs Wipro's CyberTransform and CyberShield services with CrowdStrike's Falcon platform to shift enterprise security from reactive tooling to AI-native, risk-led operations.
body:
• Wipro has launched a CISO Command Center in collaboration with CrowdStrike, announced September 9, to help enterprises shift from tool-driven security operations to an enterprise-wide, risk-led operating model.
  • The offering combines Wipro Intelligence solutions — CyberTransform and CyberShield — with the CrowdStrike Falcon platform, delivering integrated protection across endpoints, cloud, exposure management, and AI security.
  • Detection and response will be unified through a modern Security Operations Center, turning security signals into business risk intelligence that executives can act on at machine speed.
  • Wipro is also a member of CrowdStrike's Project QuiltWorks, a global coalition focused on identifying, prioritizing, and remediating frontier AI risk.

EAST BRUNSWICK, N.J. — Wipro Limited on Tuesday announced the launch of a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) Command Center, built in collaboration with cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike, aimed at rewiring how enterprises defend themselves against AI-accelerated threats.

The Command Center is designed to move enterprise security away from reactive, tool-driven operations toward what the companies describe as proactive, risk-informed cyber resilience — security strategy aligned to business priorities rather than isolated alerts.

What the Command Center does

The offering will be operationalized through Wipro Intelligence solutions — CyberTransform and CyberShield — and supported by the CrowdStrike Falcon platform. Together, they are intended to deliver integrated protection across four domains: endpoint security, cloud security, exposure management, and AI security.

https://x.com/CNBCTV18Live/status/2097644487128588405

Detection and response will be unified through a modern Security Operations Center (SOC), giving security teams a single pane of glass instead of fragmented point solutions. The pitch to chief information security officers is a shift in posture: from handling incidents as they arrive to managing risk continuously, at machine speed.

Built for AI-accelerated threats

The launch is pitched squarely at a problem boards are waking up to: artificial intelligence is compressing the timeline of cyberattacks while multiplying the attack surface across endpoints, cloud workloads, identities, and AI-driven systems.

"Cyber risk is intensifying pressure on boardroom decision-making. Threats that once remained dormant for months can now materialize within hours, driven by external triggers and AI-enabled exploitation."

— Amar Bysani, Global Practice Head for Cybersecurity and Risk Services, Wipro

"The Command Center will work with enterprises to turn security signals into business risk intelligence, enabling them to sense, prioritize, and respond at machine speed," Bysani said.

Daniel Bernard, CrowdStrike's chief business officer, said the partnership gives CISOs "the AI-native security, intelligence, and services they need to turn risk into action at machine speed and transform security into a business advantage."

How Wipro fits in

For Wipro, the Command Center anchors its consulting-led cybersecurity strategy — a move upmarket from traditional managed security services toward advisory work that shapes how enterprises think about risk. The company says the offering is further strengthened by its membership in Project QuiltWorks, CrowdStrike's global coalition focused on identifying, prioritizing, and remediating frontier AI risk.

Wipro, with more than 240,000 employees across 65 countries, says it fields over 200 CrowdStrike-trained and certified professionals and was named CrowdStrike's Americas Champion Partner of the Year. CrowdStrike, for its part, brings the Falcon platform — its cloud-native system for protecting endpoints, cloud workloads, identity, and data, built on real-time attack indicators, threat intelligence, and enriched telemetry.

What's next

The real test will be enterprise adoption: whether CISOs buy the argument that security operations should be reorganized around business risk rather than threat feeds. For India's IT services majors, the Command Center is another step up the value chain — from staffing contracts to selling AI-native security strategy directly to global boardrooms. As AI-driven attacks accelerate, the companies betting on this shift are wagering that the winners in cybersecurity services will be the ones who can translate machine-speed threats into board-speed decisions.
